copy.caption:
A chipmaker posted record profits, and about $590 billion disappeared from its market in two days.

SK Hynix reported record profits. Within 48 hours South Korea's stock market had halted trading twice and roughly $590 billion in market value was gone.

Nothing failed. That is the part worth slowing down for.

The results were a record. They just landed under elevated analyst expectations. The AI trade had already priced in something better than record, so a record was enough to trigger the drop.

That is an expectations reset, not a results failure. Two very different stories that look identical on a chart.

Here is the contrast that makes the week strange. In the same window OpenAI cut its API pricing 80%. Using AI got dramatically cheaper while paying for the machines that run it got questioned. Those two costs are moving in opposite directions.

So the real open question is not whether AI works. It is whether the buildout spending keeps paying back this fast.

Which means you watch the spending plans, not the share price. If these companies actually cut their build budgets, that is news. One bad expectations week is not a verdict.

Which would change your mind first, a falling share price or a shrinking build budget? Tell us in the comments.

SK Hynix reported record profits this week, and within 48 hours South Korea's stock market had halted trading twice while about $590 billion in market value drained away.

The results came in strong. The selloff happened because analysts had priced in something better than a record, so a record was enough to knock the price down. Markets reprice expectations like that all the time, and on a chart the move looks identical to a business stumbling, even though the two say very different things to anyone deciding what to build.

Using AI got cheaper again in the same window, with OpenAI cutting its API pricing by 80%. The infrastructure serving those calls keeps getting more expensive to build, so the AI trade now hangs on whether the buildout pays back on the timeline investors assumed.

The signal to watch from here is capital spending guidance. If companies revise their buildout plans down, the thesis changed. So far the market has only adjusted its own forecast.

If you're planning around AI capacity, which carries more weight for you, the market reaction or the next round of spending guidance?
